Subject: QBR prep: portfolio tilt + contingency scenarios

Team —

I want to kick off a short QBR prep thread focused on two things we need for the exec review next month: (1) a proposed "portfolio tilt" — how we shift capacity and go-to-market focus across Hosted / Dedicated / Private for FY28, and (2) 2–3 contingency scenarios tied to revenue/risk (best case / base / downside) with associated levers (pricing, reserved capacity, hiring pauses).

Ask: please review the attached scenario workbook (FY28_portfolio_scenarios.xlsx) and drop a brief note in this thread with:
- your recommended tilt (% revenue / % capacity targets per product line)
- one resource lever and one commercial lever we could use in a downside case
- any hard constraints (e.g., contracts, capacity, compliance work) that would block a lever

Timeline: can I get your inputs by end-of-day Wednesday 6/23? I will consolidate and circulate a one-page summary + QBR slide on Thursday 6/24.

Attachments: FY28_portfolio_scenarios.xlsx (sheet: summary + scenarios), rollup-template.csv (to standardize numbers)

Thanks —
Lauren

Subject: Re: QBR prep: portfolio tilt + contingency scenarios

Thanks Lauren — good framing. A couple quick strategic notes to guide everyone's inputs:

1) Tilt guidance: prioritize Dedicated for predictable ARR growth in 28 but only to the extent we can guarantee margins. Proposed high-level split to consider: Hosted 45%, Dedicated 35%, Private 20% (by revenue). But allow product-level exceptions for key regulated accounts.

2) Levers: for downside, prefer short-term commercial levers (temporary promos, payment deferrals) over hiring freezes in the first 30 days — hiring/hard headcount changes have long lead times and can harm delivery. For deep downside, prioritize quantization/ops efficiencies (lower unit cost) + prioritized customer support SLAs.

Constraints: Any large Dedicated commitments we sign before QBR must be tabled in the slide as a "blocker" if they exceed our forecast cadence.

I'll add a short note in the workbook later today.

— Vivek

Lauren / team —

Quick operational reality check from capacity planning:
- We have GPU reservations expiring in Q3 that would reduce our Dedicated throughput by ~18% unless we convert or extend. That shows up as a material downside lever.
- Private deployments have longer sales cycles but higher ACV; shifting more quota to Private will require an 8–12 week onboarding lift per large customer.

My inputs in the workbook (tab: ops_notes):
- Recommended tilt change for FY28: Hosted 48%, Dedicated 30%, Private 22% (leans slightly toward Hosted to preserve immediate throughput).
- Resource lever (downside): defer two non-critical infra hires (infra automation + one SRE) — this saves ~FTE costs in the near term but increases incident risk unless we prioritize runbook automation.

Attachment notes: I linked a short ops runbook draft into the Drive link for contingency work.

On constraints: Acme Industries has a pending compliance ask that could push their Private deployment into Q1 FY29 unless we greenlight an accelerated audit (costly). Marking as "customer blocker" in the workbook.

— Grace
